newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1997 economic growth seen at 4 pct-Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1997 economic growth seen at 4 pct-Malan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said he expected gross domestic product (GDP) to expand by about four percent in 1997 and even more in 1998.

"1997 is the fifth consecutive year of GDP growth and 1998 will be the sixth consecutive year of growth," Malan said. "GDP growth was three percent last year, will be around four percent this year and more than that in 1998."
Malan, who spoke at a lunch in Rio de Janeiro on the government's three-year-old anti-inflation Real Plan, said inflation would slow to seven percent in 1997.
He said government reforms aimed at reigning in the public sector deficit were fundamentally important in further consolidating the Real Plan.
"The fundamental challenges lie in the public sector," Malan said. " We are at a critical point. We have to reform pensions, we have to reform the civil service and we have to reform the tax system."

The government's reform proposals in these areas have come up against strong resistance in Brazil's conservative Congress and government officials and investors fear that time is running out for their approval in the run-up to presidential and congressional elections in October next year.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
